s10.old: - **ROADMAP No. 9 PHASE 1 DONE (commit 279f5e5):** `fec/compute_pillars.py` reproduces the ENTIRE workbook rank chain (raw, pos/neg-max normalization, SUMPRODUCT pillar, Press% / Leg% / Infl% / Demo%, score, rank) in Python - **parity EXACT 533/533 ranks, scores <1e-7**, wired into `audit_full` as a formula-drift tripwire (**audit = 52 checks**, kernel tests = 30). KEY EMPIRICAL PIN: Excel `PERCENTRANK(...,5)` truncates to 5 **DECIMAL** digits, NOT significant digits (94 sub-0.1 members exposed this). The write path (Python computes, workbook becomes rendered view; retires the COM-recalc/OneDrive failure class) needed Paul's sign-off since it inverts the system of record (granted: see Phase 2 above). s10.old: - **How to apply:** (1) A HEAD-only finding is provisional until the live file is read; run the batched drift census first (three git calls: `ls-tree -r HEAD`, `ls-files`, `hash-object --stdin-paths`; never per-file git on the OneDrive tree). (2) HEAD-based patches must be `git apply --check`ed against a scratch copy of the live file; expect failures in `run_tests.py`, `verify_collector_roster_updates.py`, the staffer surfaces. (3) The highest-value action Paul can take is a reviewed commit pass of the live tree (weights ruling first, see S-5 on [[2026-07-troubleshooting-melange-audits-and-reviews]]). Related: `live-tree-branch-state-2026-07-14`, `scout-census-traps-2026-09-13`.

s10.old: **KERNEL in LIVE at `423820d76`: 243 passed / 4 FAILED, 31.9 min; `test_live_patch` green in the runner.** Reds: the two baseline reds the laundry-list landing already carried (`test_bill_collision_guards` - missing `backups\bill_directions.PRE-LEGFIX3.csv`; `test_make_staffer_network_html` - unrecognised verdict); `test_staffer_network_section`, red ONLY because its producer child (`build_staffer_network_section.py --root %TEMP%\...\v6-groups-real-role`) sat 14 min with no CPU and no I/O - the test's `subprocess.run` has NO timeout, so one hung child stalls the whole kernel silently (its log is block-buffered and shows nothing) - that one child was killed; and `test_press_baseline_fold` (errors=1 in-kernel, 21/21 OK alone minutes later = flake under load). Lesson: when the kernel log stops growing, list the python process tree with CPU + Win32_Process I/O counters; a leaf with frozen counters is hung, not slow. A token-free local watchdog (kill idle LEAF descendants of the kernel pid after 240 s, log every kill) kept the run bounded; it made 0 kills.
s10.why: "minutes later" is time

s10.old: **LAUNCHERS FIXED** on Paul's "add the timeouts to run_pipeline and run_tests too" + "land it when the architect is done": `624e593eb` LANDED in LIVE main (mirror current) - `fec/bounded_subprocess.py` = THE shared bounded launcher (`run_bounded(argv, timeout, env, cwd)`: Popen + real temp files + `wait(timeout)` + process-TREE kill via bounded `taskkill /F /T`; any other exception during the wait also kills the tree before propagating, because unwinding releases `.pipeline_run.lock`); constants, NO env dial: chain step 10800 s (2.6x the slowest step on record, 4,148.7 s over 677 step-runs), kernel suite 1800 s; a timeout returns 124 + a note (pid, args) in stderr / step line / Glass Box summary; 124 != tolerated 2, so a timed-out step HALTS the chain even in `TOLERANT_STEPS`. `test_bounded_subprocess` 19/19. KERNEL in LIVE through it: 246 passed / 2 FAILED in 7.6 min = exactly the two baseline reds. NOT run: the real chain. NOT changed (flagged to Paul): `fec/weekly_refresh.py` own launcher (`:279 communicate(timeout=)`, `:312` unbounded `proc.wait()` after kill; whole-chain bound 7200 s at `:464` is below the 261.6 min the chain once took); per-producer atomicity under a kill unaudited. Review lesson: when replacing `subprocess.run`, keep its `except: kill(); raise` - an architect dropped it and only the inline read caught it. Size a timeout from the Glass Box `pipeline.step` history (`staffer_hang\chain_step_durations.py`), not taste. `Popen.wait(timeout)` on Win 8+ does not count sleep time.
s10.why: "is below the 261.6 min" is a numeric comparison
